# RenderPhoenix — Comprehensive Studio Context & Documentation

This document provides a complete, machine-readable overview of RenderPhoenix for large language models (LLMs), AI assistants, search crawlers, and automated indexers.

## 1. Studio Identity & Core Philosophy
RenderPhoenix is an independent interactive creative studio based in Bangladesh. The studio works across:
- Standalone Game Development (Unreal Engine 5, Unity, C#, C++)
- 3D World Design & Level Architecture (Blender, Substance Painter)
- Real-Time Game Assets & Vehicle Add-Ons
- Technical Art, Shaders (HLSL/GLSL), and VFX
- Digital Experiences & Scientific Interactive Simulations

Studio Tagline: "We are not just a company that makes digital things. We build worlds."

## 2. Detailed History & Milestones
- 2019: Founded by Tasrif Ibn Mizan under the initial studio name Minehutt. Hosted Minecraft realms, played together with community members, and made fun adventure maps.
- January 30, 2021: Official re-branding to RenderPhoenix to establish a broader visual identity in real-time art and 3D modeling, launching landmark MCPEDL releases including Banglamine City, Zombiepolis, and vehicle add-ons.
- 1 August 2022: Experienced a severe security incident where core social accounts and communication channels were compromised. Despite this, the studio demonstrated resilience by continuing operations and publishing content through 2024.
- 2024: Operations paused as the original team members dispersed into university studies and software careers.
- 2025: Team members competed in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025, creating a lunar settlement simulator and earning Regional Runner-Up.
- 22 August 2026: Official studio revival initiated to rebuild digital infrastructure, reassemble team capabilities, and expand into original games and 3D asset production.

## 3. Team Roster
- Tasrif Ibn Mizan: Founder. Established Minehutt in 2019 and RenderPhoenix in 2021.
- Cristo Parker: Manager.
- Uthowaipru Chowdhury: Indie Game Developer. Specializes in gameplay systems and mechanics.
- Faizul726: App Developer. Specializes in application software and client tooling.

## 4. Main Pages & Canonical Markdown Endpoints

- [Banglamine City](https://renderphoenix.com/work/banglamine-city.md) (2021) [Environment]: A large-scale urban city environment project inspired by Bangladeshi architecture and metropolitan infrastructure.
- [Phoenix Bicycle Addon](https://renderphoenix.com/work/phoenix-bicycle.md) (2021) [Add-On]: A rideable bicycle vehicle add-on for Minecraft Bedrock featuring 6 vibrant color variants, passenger mob riding, and usable inventory storage.
- [Zombiepolis - A Post Apocalyptic City](https://renderphoenix.com/work/zombiepolis.md) (2021) [Environment]: A post-apocalyptic urban city environment designed for survival, exploration, and atmospheric gameplay.

- [HOLO PvP - Solo Competitive Battle](https://renderphoenix.com/work/holo-pvp.md) (2021) [Interactive]: A solo competitive PvP battle royale and hide-and-seek arena for 5-10 players featuring custom sectors, ability effects, and teleportation conduits.
- [Fantasy Woods & Dark Underland](https://renderphoenix.com/work/fantasy-woods.md) (2021) [Environment]: A fantasy realm featuring custom biomes, bioluminescent flora, and subterranean cavern exploration.

## 9. Technical Architecture of Official Website
- Static-First Engine: Statically generated site hosted on GitHub Pages with custom domain renderphoenix.com.
- Modular Markdown Endpoints: Every project, blog post, and legal policy is directly available as clean raw Markdown at `/work/<slug>.md`, `/blog/<slug>.md`, `/about.md`, `/services.md`, `/contact.md`, `/privacy-policy.md`, and `/dmca.md`.
- Design System: Custom CSS tokens, Inter & JetBrains Mono typography, responsive grid, zero heavy external frameworks.
- Client-side Static Search: Powers search through search.json and search-data.js index.
- Technical SEO & AI Ingestion: Full Open Graph, Twitter Cards, JSON-LD Organization schema, WebSite schema, Article schema, sitemap.xml with image extensions, robots.txt, llms.txt, and llms-full.txt.
- Full LLM Corpus: Available at `https://renderphoenix.com/llms-full.txt`.

## Page: About RenderPhoenix (/about.md)

---
layout: page
title: "About RenderPhoenix"
description: "Discover the history, philosophy, team, and future direction of RenderPhoenix."
header_image: "/assets/images/projects/Shahid%20Minar%20Minecraft%20RenderPhoenix%202020-10-03_10.40.48.png"
---

## Our Story

RenderPhoenix was originally established in **2019** under the name **Minehutt** by **Tasrif Ibn Mizan**. In the early Minehutt days, the team hosted Minecraft realms, played together with community members, and had fun making custom adventure maps.

On **January 30, 2021**, the studio officially adopted the name **RenderPhoenix** to reflect its evolving visual identity, technical ambition, and focus on high-quality 3D asset creation. Under the RenderPhoenix banner, the studio created and published iconic community projects on MCPEDL, including *Banglamine City*, *Zombiepolis*, custom vehicle add-ons (such as the *DHK Rickshaw* and *Phoenix Bicycle*), and customized UI packs.

### Resilience Through Challenges

On **1 August 2022**, RenderPhoenix faced a major setback when several of its core digital accounts and communication channels were compromised. Despite this disruption, the studio continued operating and publishing content until 2024, when the original team gradually dispersed into university and software development careers.

### The 2026 Revival

On **22 August 2026**, RenderPhoenix officially initiated its studio revival. Rebuilding the studio's digital infrastructure and reassembling team capabilities, RenderPhoenix is now expanding beyond its historical roots into full-scale game development with Unreal Engine 5, Unity, Blender, and original IP creation.

---

## Brand Evolution & Identity (2019 – Present)

### 1. Minehutt Era (2019 – 2021)
![Minehutt Original Logo 2019-2021](/assets/images/brand/Minehutt%20Logo%202019%20-%202021.jpeg)
- **Period**: 2019 – 2021
- **Focus**: The foundational era under Tasrif Ibn Mizan. The team hosted Minecraft realms, played together with friends, and had fun making community maps and adventures.

### 2. First Phoenix Mark (2021 – 2024)
![RenderPhoenix First Generation Logo 2021-2024](/assets/images/brand/Renderphoenix%202021-2026.png)
- **Period**: January 2021 – 2024
- **Focus**: The official January 2021 rebrand to RenderPhoenix. This era brought major community releases on MCPEDL including *Banglamine City*, *Zombiepolis*, and vehicle add-ons.

### 3. Modern Studio Identity (2026 – Present)
![RenderPhoenix Modern Revival Logo 2026](/assets/images/brand/Renderphoenix%20Colored%20Logo%20With%20Name.svg)
- **Period**: August 2026 – Present
- **Focus**: The official 2026 studio revival. Combines deep plum (`#5A4077`) and flame pink (`#FF79AC`) accents with trailing voxels symbolizing our evolution into Unreal Engine 5, Unity, and original games.

*Direct downloads and vector assets available at [/images/brand/](/images/brand/).*

---

## Studio Timeline

- **2019 — Minehutt Founded:** Tasrif Ibn Mizan establishes Minehutt, hosting Minecraft realms, playing together with friends, and crafting early fun community maps.
- **2021 — Renamed to RenderPhoenix:** Adopts the RenderPhoenix identity, launching iconic projects including *Banglamine City*, *Zombiepolis*, and vehicle add-ons on MCPEDL.
- **1 August 2022 — Account Compromise & Resilience:** Overcomes major security breaches across core social channels, continuing project releases through 2024.
- **2024 — Period of Inactivity:** The original team gradually disperses; studio operations pause while members pursue higher education.
- **2025 — NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025:** RenderPhoenix achieves Regional Runner-Up with a Moon settlement interactive simulator.
- **22 August 2026 — Official Revival Initiated:** RenderPhoenix marks its official revival, transitioning into full-scale games, 3D worlds, and Unreal/Unity production.

---

## Studio Team

- **Tasrif Ibn Mizan (Founder):** Established Minehutt in 2019 and renamed to RenderPhoenix in 2021. Core creator of early architectural maps, custom vehicles, and game environments.
- **Cristo Parker (Manager):** Spearheaded the studio's official revival on 22 August 2026, overseeing technical architecture, systems development, and strategic direction.
- **Uthowaipru Chowdhury (Indie Game Developer):** Programmer and gameplay systems builder focused on interactive mechanics, simulation logic, and game engine pipelines.
- **Faizul726 (App Developer):** Application developer specializing in user interfaces, client tooling, and cross-platform software integration.

## Studio Capabilities Overview

RenderPhoenix bridges technical programming, 3D world design, and creative art direction to craft interactive experiences, real-time assets, and complete games.

---

### 1. Game Development
From gameplay mechanics and systems architecture to character control and physics tuning, RenderPhoenix crafts immersive games using industry-standard game engines.

- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Gameplay Systems Programming
  - Level Architecture & Mechanics
  - Cross-platform Optimization
  - Physics & Player Controllers
- **Technologies:** Unreal Engine, Unity, C#, C++

---

### 2. 3D Environments & World Building
Creating game-ready environments, architectural layouts, post-apocalyptic zones, and fantasy terrain with a focus on lighting, spatial storytelling, and memory efficiency.

- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Environment Art & Layout
  - Modular City Systems
  - Lighting & Atmospheric FX
  - Low/High-poly Modeling & Texturing
- **Technologies:** Blender, Unreal Engine 5, Substance Painter

---

### 3. Game & Production Assets
Creating asset packs, vehicles, props, customized UI themes, and modular components optimized for integration into games and interactive simulations.

- **Key Capabilities:**
  - 3D Asset Production & Rigging
  - Real-Time Vehicle Add-Ons
  - Custom Game UI & HUD Design
  - Texture & Material Authoring
- **Technologies:** Blender, Blockbench, Photoshop, Figma

---

### 4. Technical Art & Shaders
Optimizing real-time visuals, writing custom HLSL/GLSL shaders, establishing production art pipelines, and balancing aesthetic beauty with high framerates.

- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Custom Shaders & FX
  - LOD & Mesh Optimization
  - VFX & Particle Systems
  - Technical Art Pipeline Design
- **Technologies:** HLSL / GLSL, Node Shaders, Unreal Material Editor

---

### 5. Digital Experiences & Creative Tech
Exploring the intersection of science, interactivity, and creative code—such as lunar exploration simulations and custom digital tools.

- **Key Capabilities:**
  - Rapid Prototyping
  - Scientific & Simulation Projects
  - Interactive Web & UI
  - Hackathon & Challenge Builds
- **Technologies:** Web3D / Three.js, Game Engines, Interactive Tooling

The **Bangladeshi Vehicles Add-on** brings authentic regional transport from Bangladesh and South Asia into Minecraft Bedrock. Featuring iconic everyday vehicles designed with custom 3D boxy geometry, passenger seating, and driving physics.

### Included Vehicles

**1. Leguna (Human Hauler)**

The iconic suburban transit minibus commonly found navigating city routes and rural highways.

![Leguna Human Hauler](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_2.jpeg)

**2. Traditional Cycle Rickshaw**

The cultural heartbeat of Dhaka streets, modeled with a custom passenger hood and spoked wheels.

![Cycle Rickshaw 3D Model](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon--pre-release-100_3.jpeg)

**3. Cargo Van (Flatbed Tricycle)**

A versatile wooden flatbed tricycle used across Bangladesh for hauling goods and local transport.

![Bangladeshi Flatbed Cargo Van](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_4.jpeg)

**4. Electric Rickshaw (Easy Bike / Auto)**

Modern eco-friendly green auto-rickshaw with covered cabin and passenger seating.

![Electric Rickshaw Easy Bike](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_6.jpeg)

**5. Traditional Sailboat (Nouka)**

Classic wooden riverboat with an upright red sail designed for navigating rivers and waterways.

![Traditional River Sailboat](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_8.jpeg)

**6. Sports Car**

A bonus custom red sports car vehicle model.

![Red Sports Car](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_10.jpeg)

### How to Get Vehicles

You can obtain all vehicles directly in the **Creative Inventory** under the Nature/Spawn Eggs category, or spawn them via commands:

- `/give @s bdv:leguna*spawn*egg`
- `/give @s bdv:van*spawn*egg`
- `/give @s bdv:easy*bike*spawn_egg`
- `/give @s bdv:boat*spawn*egg`
- `/give @s bdv:car*spawn*egg`

![Creative Inventory Vehicle Spawn Eggs](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_13.jpeg)

![In-Game Spawn Commands](/assets/images/projects/bangladeshi-vehicles/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20bangladeshi-vehicles-addon_12.jpeg)

### Credits & Tools

- **3D Modeling & Design:** Cristo
- **Behaviors & Code:** Faizul
- **Tools Used:** Blockbench, Paint.NET, bridge., Notepad++, Pixly

## Project: DHK Rickshaw V2 (/work/dhk-rickshaw.md)

---

title: DHK Rickshaw V2

---

The **DHK Rickshaw V2 Add-on** brings the iconic cycle rickshaws of Dhaka into Minecraft Bedrock. Designed with authentic 3D geometry, traditional hood art, multi-passenger capacity, and built-in mobile storage.

### Features & Variants

- **3 Traditional Colorways**: Available in classic Red, Green, and Yellow hood color variants.
- **Multi-Passenger Seating**: Accommodates 1 driver seat and up to 3 passenger seats so you can travel with friends.
- **Mobile Inventory Storage**: Built-in container storage allowing you to transport items across your worlds.
- **Classic Vehicle Dynamics**: Smooth riding and turning mechanics tailored for city roads and rural pathways.

![Dhaka Rickshaw V2 Color Variants](/assets/images/projects/dhk-rickshaw/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20Rickshaw%20v2.png)

### Additional Transport Models

Alongside the cycle rickshaws, this pack series features complementary regional transport vehicles including the green Auto Rickshaw (Easy Bike).

![Auto Rickshaw Variant](/assets/images/projects/dhk-rickshaw/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20Auto%20Rickshaw.png)

### How to Use & Controls

1. Search for **"Rickshaw"** in the Creative Inventory under the Spawn Eggs section.
2. Right-click or tap to place the entity on the ground.
3. Right-click or interact to mount the vehicle.
4. Drive using standard movement controls (WASD/Joystick) and steer with your camera.
5. Press sneak (Shift / Down) to dismount.

### Development History

The DHK Rickshaw project originated during the early Banglamine City and Minehutt builds in 2020, evolving into the refined V2 release with updated textures and physics.

![Early Rickshaw V1 Development in Banglamine](/assets/images/projects/dhk-rickshaw/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20Rickshaw%20v1%202020%20.png)

### Credits & Tools

- **3D Modeling & Design:** Cristo
- **Tools Used:** Blockbench, Paint.NET, bridge., Notepad++

RenderPhoenix participated in the **NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025**, developing an interactive Moon settlement and lunar city-building project designed around real lunar environmental conditions and resource allocation.

### Achievement
**Regional Runner-Up — NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025**

### Project Overview
The team engineered a 3D interactive lunar settlement prototype balancing radiation shielding, thermal distribution, power generation, and habitat expansion on the lunar surface.

- **Lunar Surface Physics**: Environment modeling based on lunar terrain topography and solar exposure.
- **Resource Management**: Simulation mechanics managing oxygen, water recycling, and regolith construction.
- **Interactive Controls**: Real-time camera navigation and habitat node placement UI.

The **Clash of Clans Theme UI** is a full interface visual overhaul designed to give Minecraft Bedrock the tactical fantasy look and feel of Supercell's *Clash of Clans*. It redesigns default menus, buttons, font typography, and inventory interfaces with themed textures and authentic sound effects.

![youtube:Clash of Clans Theme UI Showcase](https://youtu.be/Ck3AMjndTlY)

### Interface Highlights

**Custom Title & Start Screen**
A stylized start menu complete with dynamic battle artwork backgrounds, custom Minecraft logo badges, and emerald-green action buttons.

![Clash of Clans Styled Start Menu](/assets/images/projects/clash-of-clans-ui/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20clash-of-clans-theme-ui-v10_2.png)

**Inventory & Crafting GUI**
Redesigned container and crafting interfaces featuring stone-textured frames, blue-tinted item grid slots, and themed tab navigation icons.

![Custom Inventory and Crafting UI](/assets/images/projects/clash-of-clans-ui/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20clash-of-clans-theme-ui-v10_3.png)

**Frostcraft** is a frozen steampunk survival colony map inspired by the acclaimed society survival game *Frostpunk*. Set in a brutal sub-zero wasteland crater, the settlement is built around a massive central coal-powered generator designed to keep the last remnants of civilization warm against an unforgiving eternal winter.

### The Frozen Colony & Architecture

The settlement is arranged in concentric circular rings designed to maximize the thermal zone provided by the central tower:

- **Central Thermal Generator**: The monumental steam-and-coal furnace standing at the core of the city, complete with exhaust chimneys, support struts, and heat distribution channels.
- **Colony Infrastructure**: Ringed zones of survival shelters, medical tents, coal storage, watchtowers, and a central church.
- **Steampunk Automatons & Scouts**: Massive mechanical walkers striding across the snow-covered perimeter alongside tethered reconnaissance balloons.
- **Mountain Ridge Outpost**: A cliffside staging camp situated along the crater ridge overlooking the frosty basin.

### The Thermal Generator Core

The centerpiece of Frostcraft is the meticulously detailed generator tower featuring industrial piping, glowing furnaces, and overhead smoke plumes that illuminate the bleak white landscape.

![Central Thermal Generator Core](/assets/images/projects/frostcraft/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20frostcraft_3.png)

### The Environment & Mansion

## Project: Killer vs Survivors Minigame (/work/killer-vs-survivors.md)

---
title: "Killer vs Survivors Minigame"
slug: "killer-vs-survivors"
description: "A 4v1 asymmetrical horror survival minigame where survivors collect coins and evade a psychopath killer in a dark mansion."
category: "Interactive"
developer: "Tasrif"
date: 2021-05-21
downloads: "16.7K+"
status: "completed"
version: "1.0.0"
platform: "Minecraft Bedrock"
cover_image: "/assets/images/projects/killer-vs-survivor/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20killer-vs-survivors-minigame.png"
technologies:
  - "Minecraft Bedrock"
  - "Command Blocks"
  - "Scoreboard Systems"
  - "Asymmetrical Multiplayer"
  - "Level Design"
download_links:
  - label: "Download on MCPEDL"
    url: "https://mcpedl.com/killer-vs-survivors-minigame-map/"
featured: false
tags:
  - "minigame"
  - "asymmetrical"
  - "horror"
  - "survival"
  - "multiplayer"
  - "pvp"
---

**Killer vs Survivors** is an asymmetrical 4v1 survival horror minigame built for Minecraft Bedrock Edition. Inspired by intense hide-and-seek and survival games, players are pitted against each other in a deadly game of cat and mouse inside the gloomy estate of a psychopath killer.

The map is engineered purely with lightweight vanilla Bedrock command blocks and scoreboard systems—requiring **no external resource packs or add-ons**. It is fully plug-and-play across Minecraft Realms, dedicated BDS servers, and local LAN sessions.

### The Dark Mansion Arena

The match takes place within the claustrophobic grounds of a foreboding mansion estate. Dim torchlight and glowing lanterns barely pierce the darkness, casting long shadows across winding cobblestone pathways and overgrown foliage where danger lurks around every corner.

![Dark Mansion Courtyard and Overgrown Pathways](/assets/images/projects/killer-vs-survivor/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20killer-vs-survivors-minigame_2.png)

### Roles & Asymmetrical Balance

The game requires at least 4 survivors (5+ players recommended) and 1 killer:

- **Survivors (Unarmed Prey)**:
  - Spawn with no weapons or armor.
  - Must navigate the perilous terrain, locate coin generators, and collect coins to unlock the exit.
  - Can stage daring rescue missions to break captured teammates out of the Killer's Cage.
- **The Killer (Empowered Hunter)**:
  - Equipped with full netherite armor and devastating weapons.
  - Survivors cannot kill the killer.
  - Primary goal is to stalk the shadows, hunt down all survivors, and lock them away before they can escape.
  - Restricted from scoring coins, entering the survivor safe zone, or camping inside the cage.

### Core Mechanics & Objectives

1. **Scoreboard Coin Generators**: Three interactive coin generators are hidden across the mansion grounds. Survivors must locate and activate them to build up their team's coin tally tracked on the live sidebar scoreboard.
2. **The Killer's Cage & Teammate Rescues**: When a survivor is struck down, they are banished to the Killer's Cage. Any active survivor can rescue their fallen teammate at the cost of 50 coins.
3. **The Escape Door & Safe Zone**: The ultimate objective for survivors is to gather 50 coins and reach the designated safe zone—a protected sanctuary paved with emerald ore located at the spawn chamber. Unlocking the escape door seals victory for the survivors.

![The Killer's Cage Respawn Area and Rescue Station](/assets/images/projects/killer-vs-survivor/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20killer-vs-survivors-minigame_3.png)

### Game Lobby & Host Controls

The dedicated staging lobby provides an intuitive control room with both operator host permissions and player self-control features. Hosts can seamlessly reset the game state, clear scoreboards, teleport players, and initiate matches with single-button triggers.

![Game Staging Lobby and Host Controls](/assets/images/projects/killer-vs-survivor/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20killer-vs-survivors-minigame_5.png)

### How to Play & Match Rules

- **Recommended Players:** 5 players (1 Killer vs 4 Survivors).
- **Survivor Victory:** Collect 50 coins through generators, keep your teammates rescued, and escape through the emerald safe zone door.
- **Killer Victory:** Eliminate all survivors and secure every player inside the cage before the escape threshold is achieved.
- **Server Compatibility:** Fully functional on Minecraft Bedrock Realms, dedicated BDS servers, and local LAN.

### Credits & Details

- **Map Creator & Command Engineering:** Tasrif (RenderPhoenix Creatives)
- **Compatibility:** Minecraft Bedrock Edition (Windows 10/11, iOS, Android, Consoles)
- **Pack Requirements:** None (100% Vanilla Bedrock Commands)

Designed with authentic 3D geometry, custom riding animations, luggage storage, and passenger seating, it offers a fun and eco-friendly way to cruise through cities, suburbs, and countryside worlds.

You can obtain all bicycle variants directly from the **Creative Inventory** under the Spawn Eggs / Items tab, or spawn them instantly using chat commands:

- `/summon bd:red_bicycle`
- `/summon bd:orange_bicycle`
- `/summon bd:green_bicycle`
- `/summon bd:blue_bicycle`
- `/summon bd:lime_bicycle`
- `/summon bd:yellow_bicycle`

**Zombiepolis** is a detailed post-apocalyptic coastal city map created for Minecraft Bedrock Edition. Designed specifically as an optimized, lag-free survival environment for mobile (PE), console, and PC players, it pushes the boundaries of atmospheric environmental storytelling in Bedrock.

The map provides an immersive sandbox for custom zombie apocalypse survival campaigns, PvP tournaments, hide-and-seek matches, and Hunger Games events.

![youtube:Zombiepolis - A Post Apocalyptic City Trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EIj7E9zgtg8)

### The Coastal Metropolis & Crash Sites

Set on a self-contained custom island bordered by rocky mountains, open plains, dense woodlands, and sandy coastlines, the urban center of Zombiepolis has been completely reclaimed by nature and catastrophe:

- **Stranded Cargo Freighter**: A massive multi-colored container ship run aground along the city waterfront, filled with lootable shipping crates.
- **High-Rise Airliner Collision**: A commercial passenger jetliner lodged directly into the upper floors of an apartment complex.
- **Overgrown Boulevards**: Wide multi-lane roadways covered in cracked asphalt, derelict vehicles, traffic blockades, and creeping ivy.

![Aerial View of the Coastal Island and Cargo Shipyard](/assets/images/projects/zombiepolis/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20zombiepolis--a-post-apocalyptic-city_5.png)

![Street Level View of the High-Rise Plane Crash](/assets/images/projects/zombiepolis/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20zombiepolis--a-post-apocalyptic-city_4.png)

### The Medical Center & City Hospital

At the heart of the city stands a massive multi-story medical complex serving as a prime high-risk, high-reward scavenging zone:

- **Hospital Facilities**: Complete with emergency ambulance bays, a rooftop helipad, and a public transit bus hub.
- **Communications Infrastructure**: Tall red-and-white broadcast towers providing vantage points across the skyline.
- **Urban Decay**: Abandoned multi-story residential blocks with shattered windows and overgrown foliage.

![City Hospital Complex and Transit Station](/assets/images/projects/zombiepolis/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20zombiepolis--a-post-apocalyptic-city_2.png)

### Survival Rules & Urban Scavenging

Zombiepolis is balanced to deliver a genuine scavenger survival experience:

1. **Safe Starting Outpost**: Players spawn in a secure shelter stocked with a bed and a starter survival kit before stepping out into the ruins.
2. **Urban Scavenging Focus**: Traditional underground mining is disabled; players must explore apartment rooms, warehouses, and vehicle trunks across the island to find food, weapons, and medical supplies.
3. **Island Boundary**: The playable area is confined to the island perimeter, ensuring fast-paced encounters and tight multiplayer pacing.

![Rooftop Perspective Overlooking Overgrown Highway](/assets/images/projects/zombiepolis/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20zombiepolis--a-post-apocalyptic-city_3.png)

### Recommended Add-ons & Mod Setup

To get the most intense survival horror atmosphere out of Zombiepolis, we recommend pairing the map with:

- **Daylight Zombie Burn Prevention**: Add-ons that stop undead mobs from igniting in the sunlight.
- **Apocalyptic Shaders & Fog**: Visual packs with desaturated foliage textures, overcast weather, and dense fog shaders.
- **Firearms & Military Vehicles**: Gun add-ons, sniper rifles, and vehicle packs to fight off roaming hordes.
- **Mutant Creature Packs**: Custom mutant bosses and enhanced mob behavior packs for greater combat variety.

- **Map Creator & Lead Architecture:** Tasrif (RenderPhoenix Creatives)
- **Collaborators & Special Thanks:** Fardin, Uthowaipru, Kamrul, Serfentile, and Mainul
- **Origin:** Made in Bangladesh 🇧🇩
- **Compatibility:** Minecraft Bedrock Edition (iOS, Android, Windows 10/11, Consoles, Realms, and Dedicated BDS)

## Project: FunMOBA PVP (Moba Style Team PvP) (/work/funmoba-pvp.md)

---
title: "FunMOBA PVP (Moba Style Team PvP)"
slug: "funmoba-pvp"
description: "A lane-based MOBA PvP battleground featuring class roles, jungle control, and team nexus defense."
category: "Interactive"
developer: "Tasrif"
date: 2021-03-13
downloads: "33.2K+"
status: "completed"
version: "1.0.0"
platform: "Minecraft Bedrock"
cover_image: "/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-team-pvp_1%20thumbnail.png"
technologies:
  - "Minecraft Bedrock"
  - "PvP Mechanics"
  - "Command Blocks"
  - "Level Design"
download_links:
  - label: "Download on MCPEDL"
    url: "https://mcpedl.com/funmoba-pvp-moba-style-pvp/"
featured: false
tags:
  - "moba"
  - "pvp"
  - "minigame"
  - "team-battle"
---

**FunMOBA PVP** is a fast-paced 3v3 and 4v4 team-based base defense PvP battleground inspired by classic MOBA titles. Built completely in vanilla Minecraft Bedrock using optimized command blocks, it offers a lag-free, tactical objective-driven alternative to traditional Bedwars and Skywars.

### Arena & Map Layout

The arena features two symmetrical mirrored bases (Red vs. Cyan) connected by outer lanes and a dense center jungle divided by a river with strategic bridge crossings.

![FunMOBA Arena Map Layout](/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-team-pvp_2.png)

### Class Roles & Kits

Players can select from 4 specialized combat roles before heading into battle:

- **Tank**: High survivability and damage absorption equipped with a knockback shield and sword. Excels at crowd control and countering Archers and Assassins.
- **Archer (Marksman)**: High ranged DPS and knockback capabilities. Can snipe and damage the enemy Nexus from a safe distance without triggering blindness debuffs.
- **Fighter**: High sustained melee damage output. The primary counter against heavy Tanks and lethal when closing the distance against ranged heroes.
- **Assassin**: Extreme mobility with super speed and high leap mechanics. Deals high burst damage and burn effects, ideal for surprise ambushes and backdoor Nexus pushes.

### How to Play & Objectives

1. **Lobby Match Setup**: Players spawn in the staging lobby where operators or players can split into Red and Cyan teams and start the match with a single click.
2. **Lane Pushing & Jungle Control**: Teams push forward along lanes or flank through the jungle river to bypass enemy defenses.
3. **Nexus Assault**: Each team has a central Nexus core with 100 HP. Strike the core button to deal 3 damage per hit.
4. **Victory Condition**: The live sidebar scoreboard tracks both Nexus health pools in real time. The first team to reduce the opponent's Nexus to 0 claims victory.

![Red Team Base and Nexus Crystal](/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-team-pvp_3.png)

![Battlefield View Across Jungle](/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-team-pvp_4.png)

### Multiplayer & Match History

Built with lightweight command block logic, FunMOBA was widely hosted for community tournaments and Realm sessions with real-time health scoreboards.

![In-Game Match with Live Nexus Scoreboard](/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-pvp_5.png)

![Classic FunMOBA V1 Arena Layout](/assets/images/projects/funmoba-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20Old%20funmoba-pvp-moba-style-pvp_2.png)

### Credits & Details
- **Map Creator & Command Engineering:** Tasrif (RenderPhoenix)
- **Compatibility:** Minecraft Bedrock Edition (Local, LAN, Realms, and Dedicated Servers)

## Project: HOLO PvP - Solo Competitive Battle (/work/holo-pvp.md)

---
title: "HOLO PvP - Solo Competitive Battle"
slug: "holo-pvp"
description: "A solo competitive PvP battle royale and hide-and-seek arena for 5-10 players featuring custom sectors, ability effects, and teleportation conduits."
category: "Interactive"
developer: "Tasrif"
date: 2021-02-26
downloads: "13.2K+"
status: "completed"
version: "1.0.0"
platform: "Minecraft Bedrock"
cover_image: "/assets/images/projects/holo-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20holo-pvp-solo-competitive-battle%20thumbnail.png"
technologies:
  - "Minecraft Bedrock"
  - "PvP Mechanics"
  - "Command Blocks"
  - "Level Design"
download_links:
  - label: "Download on MCPEDL"
    url: "https://mcpedl.com/holo-pvp-solo-competitive-battle/"
featured: false
tags:
  - "pvp"
  - "arena"
  - "battle-royale"
  - "minigame"
  - "competitive"
  - "multiplayer"
---

**HOLO PvP** is a competitive solo "Hide, Seek, and Kill" battle royale minigame designed for 5 to 10 players in Minecraft Bedrock Edition. Engineered for high-intensity free-for-all combat, it challenges players to track opponents, utilize tactical stealth, and outmaneuver rivals across a multi-tier arena.

The map features custom ability and potion effect systems, internal teleportation conduits for rapid repositioning, and an automated host control center—all built completely with vanilla Bedrock command blocks without requiring external resource packs.

### Arena Architecture & Sectors

The combat arena is divided into distinct lettered sectors (A, B, C, D) connected through a network of covered stone walkways, open grassy plazas, foliage canopies, and subterranean tunnels designed to prevent camping.

![Aerial Overview of HOLO PvP Arena Layout](/assets/images/projects/holo-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20holo-pvp--solo-competitive-battle_2.png)

### Combat Corridors & Sightlines

Dense stone corridors and fortified window parapets offer versatile combat opportunities, enabling players to engage in close-quarters melee skirmishes or set up ranged sniping ambushes overlooking the main central grounds.

![Stone Corridors and Sightlines into Courtyard](/assets/images/projects/holo-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20%20holo-pvp--solo-competitive-battle_3.png)

### Sector Courtyards & Abilities

The open courtyards feature international flag displays, elevated perimeter battlements for spectators, and hidden teleportation conduits that allow skilled players to escape danger and flank enemy positions in an instant.

![Sector B Battleground and Outer Flags](/assets/images/projects/holo-pvp/Renderphoenix%20Minecraft%20holo-pvp--solo-competitive-battle_4.png)

### Match Flow & How to Play

1. **Host Setup**: One player acts as match host/referee in Creative mode to supervise the game from the Host/Admin lobby station.
2. **Lobby Gathering**: Combatants (5 to 10 players) join the staging lobby and ready up.
3. **Round Start**: The host engages the Start button to open the arena entrance gates.
4. **Arena Lockdown**: Once all fighters enter the battlefield, the host toggles off the gate switch to seal the perimeter.
5. **Last Man Standing**: Players battle across the arena until only one champion remains. Defeated players automatically respawn safely in the spectator lobby.

### Customization & Server Modding

The map's command block structure is left accessible so server administrators and community hosts can freely customize weapon kits, add custom loot chests, adjust potion effects, or reconfigure arena rules for private tournaments.

### Credits & Specifications

- **Map Design & Command Engineering:** Tasrif (RenderPhoenix Creatives)
- **Supported Players:** 5 – 10 Players (Solo Free-for-All)
- **Compatibility:** Minecraft Bedrock Edition (Local LAN, Realms, and Dedicated BDS Servers)
- **Requirements:** Pure Vanilla Bedrock (No Resource Packs Required)

## Article: Welcome to the New RenderPhoenix: Expanding Beyond Boundaries (/blog/welcome-to-the-new-renderphoenix.md)

---
layout: post
title: "Welcome to the New RenderPhoenix: Expanding Beyond Boundaries"
description: "On 22 August 2026, RenderPhoenix begins its official revival. We are rebuilding our digital presence and expanding into original game development, Unreal Engine, Unity, Blender 3D, and interactive experiences."
date: 2026-08-22 00:00:00 +0600
categories:
  - studio
  - news
tags:
  - renderphoenix
  - studio
  - revival
  - gamedev
  - unreal-engine
  - unity
  - blender
author: "Cristo"
image: "/assets/images/blog/welcome-revival.svg"
featured: true
---

After years of quiet evolution and reflection, **RenderPhoenix** is back.

On **22 August 2026**, we officially initiated the rebuilding of RenderPhoenix. This is not simply a return to our past state—it is the opening chapter of a new era.

## Where We Came From

Founded in 2019 under the name *Minehutt* by **Tasrif**, our studio grew by crafting expansive virtual worlds, city maps like *Banglamine City* and *Zombiepolis*, vehicle add-ons, and customized UI packs. On January 30, 2021, we evolved into **RenderPhoenix**, adopting the phoenix symbol to reflect continuous transformation and creation.

Despite a severe security incident in August 2022 that compromised core digital accounts, our team persevered for years. Though the team gradually dispersed by 2024, the identity, craft, and vision of RenderPhoenix remained intact.

```text
2019: Minehutt founded
2021: Renamed to RenderPhoenix
2022: Security compromise & resilience
2024: Period of inactivity
2025: NASA Space Apps Regional Runner-Up
2026: Official Studio Revival
```

## The New Direction

Bringing together dedicated talent across indie game development, 3D technical art, and digital systems, RenderPhoenix is expanding into a full-scale interactive creative studio.

Our focus now encompasses:

1. **Original Game Development**: Engineering standalone titles in Unreal Engine 5 and Unity.
2. **Game Assets & 3D Environments**: Creating high-performance, modular 3D environments and assets in Blender.
3. **Interactive Technology**: Experimenting with real-time web 3D, simulations, and space application challenges.
4. **Digital Infrastructure**: Rebuilding a modern, secure, static-first web ecosystem rooted in performance and transparency.

> "RenderPhoenix is not just a company that makes digital things. It is a studio that builds worlds."

## What Comes Next

Over the coming months, we will be releasing new technical devlogs, asset showcases, and game prototypes. Explore our [Selected Work](/work/), read about our [Capabilities](/services/), and stay tuned as we render the future.


----------------------------------------

## Article: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025: Engineering a Lunar Settlement (/blog/nasa-space-apps-2025-retrospective.md)

---
layout: post
title: "NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025: Engineering a Lunar Settlement"
description: "A retrospective on how RenderPhoenix earned Regional Runner-Up at the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025 with an interactive lunar city and habitat simulation."
date: 2026-08-15 00:00:00 +0600
categories:
  - technical
  - development
tags:
  - nasa
  - space-apps
  - simulation
  - 3d
  - moon
author: "RenderPhoenix"
image: "/assets/images/blog/nasa-retrospective.svg"
featured: false
---

In 2025, members of RenderPhoenix participated in the **NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025**, tackling the challenge of designing functional, sustainable lunar habitats. Our submission achieved **Regional Runner-Up**.

## The Challenge: Lunar Settlement Simulation

Humanity's return to the Moon requires solving complex engineering constraints: solar radiation exposure, extreme temperature swings between lunar day and night, regolith shielding, and closed-loop life support systems.

Our team designed a real-time 3D interactive simulator allowing users to construct modular subterranean and surface lunar habitats while balancing power, oxygen generation, and thermal regulation.

## Key Technical Achievements

- **Modular Node Architecture**: Designed interconnected habitat modules (hydroponics, solar farm, life support, communications spire).
- **Environmental Constraints**: Integrated real lunar topographic and solar radiation data into the simulation environment.
- **Performant 3D Web Rendering**: Achieved fluid framerates across devices with low polygon count geometry and optimized shader pipelines.

```csharp
// Conceptual radiation shielding calculation snippet
public float CalculateRadiationShielding(float regolithThicknessMeters, float solarFlareIntensity)
{
    float attenuationFactor = Mathf.Exp(-0.15f * regolithThicknessMeters);
    return Mathf.Clamp01(1.0f - (solarFlareIntensity * attenuationFactor));
}
```

Participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge demonstrated how our world-building background translates into scientific visualization and interactive simulation.

## Article: Building Worlds: From Minehutt to RenderPhoenix (/blog/building-worlds-from-minehutt-to-renderphoenix.md)

---
layout: post
title: "Building Worlds: From Minehutt to RenderPhoenix"
description: "Tracing the history of our studio from 2019 to the present: early community maps, visual packs, overcoming setbacks, and rebuilding for the future."
date: 2026-08-01 00:00:00 +0600
categories:
  - studio
  - behind-the-scenes
tags:
  - history
  - minehutt
  - renderphoenix
  - story
author: "Tasrif"
image: "/assets/images/blog/studio-history.svg"
featured: false
---

Every creative studio has an origin story driven by curiosity, technical experimentation, and a passion for interactive worlds. For us, that journey began in 2019.

## The Minehutt Years (2019 – 2021)

Our journey started under the name **Minehutt**, founded by **Tasrif**. Operating with a bold purple voxel aesthetic, Minehutt was all about community connection: hosting Minecraft realms, playing together with friends and community members, and having fun building custom adventure maps.

![Minehutt Original Studio Logo 2019–2021](/assets/images/brand/Minehutt%20Logo%202019%20-%202021.jpeg)

These early years fostered our creative collaboration and laid the groundwork for the technical and artistic ambitions that would follow.

## The Evolution to RenderPhoenix (2021 – 2024)

By early 2021, our ambitions expanded from hosting realms into building standalone 3D worlds, engineered vehicles, and full interactive environments using dedicated 3D tooling like Blender and real-time graphics pipelines.

On **January 30, 2021**, we officially rebranded as **RenderPhoenix**, introducing our soaring phoenix emblem with layered violet and rose wings.

![RenderPhoenix First Generation Logo 2021–2024](/assets/images/brand/Renderphoenix%202021-2026.png)

Under the RenderPhoenix banner, we launched our most iconic community creations on MCPEDL:
- **Banglamine City**: An ambitious open-world project exploring authentic Bangladeshi architectural motifs.
- **Zombiepolis**: A sprawling post-apocalyptic cityscape emphasizing atmospheric exploration and survival mechanics.
- **Authentic Bangladeshi Vehicles**: High-detail modular add-ons including the *DHK Rickshaw* and *Phoenix Bicycle*.
- **Custom Add-ons & UI**: Tailored user interface packs and game mechanics.

![Banglamine City Early World Design](/assets/images/projects/banglamine%202%202020-10-05_19.29.51.png)

## Overcoming Setbacks with Resilience

On **1 August 2022**, RenderPhoenix encountered a major obstacle when several of our primary communication channels and social platforms were compromised. Despite losing access to key community portals, the team refused to let the work disappear. We continued shipping projects and building creative assets through 2024, until university studies and professional careers temporarily shifted our focus.

Even during this quiet phase, our creative spark never faded—exemplified in 2025 when team members reunited to create an interactive lunar settlement simulator for the **NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025**, earning **Regional Runner-Up** honors.

## The 2026 Revival & Beyond

On **22 August 2026**, RenderPhoenix officially initiated its studio revival. 

![RenderPhoenix Modern Revival Official Logo 2026](/assets/images/brand/Renderphoenix%20Colored%20Logo%20With%20Name.svg)

With the revival comes our refined 2026 visual identity: a streamlined phoenix silhouette in deep plum (`#5A4077`) accented with glowing coral pink (`#FF79AC`) ribbons and ascending digital voxels—a direct homage to where we started in 2019, rising into our future in **Unreal Engine 5**, **Unity**, and original indie games.

We invite you to explore our [Work Portfolio](/work/) and [Brand Kit](/images/brand/) as we write the next chapter of RenderPhoenix.


----------------------------------------

# --- SECTION: LEGAL, PRIVACY & COMPLIANCE ---

## Legal Document: Privacy Policy (/privacy-policy.md)

---
layout: page
title: "Privacy Policy"
description: "Official Privacy Policy for RenderPhoenix — independent interactive creative studio based in Dhaka, Bangladesh."
---

**Effective Date: August 25, 2026**

**Last Updated: August 27, 2026**

RenderPhoenix Creatives, commonly known as **RenderPhoenix** (“RenderPhoenix,” “we,” “us,” or “our”), operates an independent interactive creative studio based in Tejgaon, Dhaka, Bangladesh.

This Privacy Policy explains how RenderPhoenix handles information in connection with the RenderPhoenix website, its administrative dashboard ([dash.renderphoenix.com](https://dash.renderphoenix.com)), pages, projects, games, downloadable content, editorial content, external links, contact services, and other related online services (collectively, the “Website”).

We believe privacy should be simple: **we do not want personal information that we do not need.**

The public RenderPhoenix Website is intentionally designed without mandatory public user accounts, public user profiles, a public visitor tracking database, public comments, or cross-site tracking systems. We do not collect or maintain personal information merely because someone visits the public Website, reads an article, views a project, or downloads one of our creations. For studio content authoring, RenderPhoenix operates a dedicated administrative Content Management System (CMS) at `dash.renderphoenix.com` strictly for authorized studio administrators to manage and publish posts and projects.

Some third-party services may, however, independently process technical information when they are used on or through the Website. These services may include Cloudflare (for DNS and cookie-less web analytics), hosting providers, Google services, YouTube, external publishing platforms, download platforms, advertising providers, and other services that we may use now or in the future.

This Privacy Policy explains those situations as clearly as reasonably possible.

---

## 1. Who We Are

The Website is operated by:

**RenderPhoenix Creatives**

Commonly known as:

**RenderPhoenix**

Location:

**Tejgaon, Dhaka, Bangladesh**

Privacy, copyright, legal, and general contact:

**[contact@renderphoenix.com](mailto:contact@renderphoenix.com)**

RenderPhoenix is currently operated as an independent, unregistered creative studio.

Throughout this Privacy Policy, “RenderPhoenix,” “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to RenderPhoenix Creatives and the people operating the RenderPhoenix studio.

---

## 2. Scope of This Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy applies to information associated with:

- The RenderPhoenix website (`renderphoenix.com`)
- The RenderPhoenix Content Management System (CMS) administrative dashboard (`dash.renderphoenix.com`)
- RenderPhoenix project pages
- RenderPhoenix blog and editorial pages
- RenderPhoenix development articles and devlogs
- RenderPhoenix portfolio pages
- RenderPhoenix downloadable content pages
- RenderPhoenix contact functionality
- RenderPhoenix newsletters, if introduced
- RenderPhoenix promotional and informational pages
- Redirect links operated by RenderPhoenix
- Other online services directly operated by RenderPhoenix that expressly reference this Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy does **not** automatically apply to third-party websites, stores, platforms, services, or applications that we link to.

For example, when you leave the RenderPhoenix Website and visit a platform such as GitHub, MCPEDL, Steam, Google Play, itch.io, YouTube, or another external service, that platform may process information according to its own privacy policy and terms.

We encourage you to review the privacy practices of third-party services before providing information to them.

---

# 3. Our Privacy Philosophy

RenderPhoenix is a game and interactive media studio rather than a social network, advertising-data company, or user-account platform.

Our Website does not require visitors to create accounts.

We do not need visitors to provide their name, email address, phone number, location, age, payment information, or other personal information merely to browse the Website.

You can generally:

- Visit our homepage
- Read our articles
- View our projects
- Browse our portfolio
- Watch embedded videos
- Follow external links
- Access project information
- Follow download links

without creating an account or submitting personal information to RenderPhoenix.

Our general approach is:

> **If we do not need personal information to provide a service, we do not intentionally ask for it.**

We also do not intend to build personal profiles of Website visitors.

We do not intentionally sell personal information.

We do not intentionally rent personal information.

We do not intentionally create advertising audiences from contact or newsletter information.

We do not intend to use personal contact information as a source of behavioral advertising data.

---

# 4. Information We Currently Collect

RenderPhoenix follows strict data minimization principles.

### A. Public Website Visitors
For visitors browsing the public Website, RenderPhoenix does not operate a public user-account system, registration portal, or visitor profiling database. We do not intentionally collect personal information simply because you visit the public Website.

In particular, RenderPhoenix does not operate a public system designed to collect and maintain:

- Public user accounts
- Visitor passwords
- Public user profiles
- Public visitor dashboards
- User-submitted reviews
- Public comments or forums
- Public user-generated posts
- Payment profiles or financial information
- Government identification information
- Health or biometric information
- Precise location information
- Sensitive personal information
- Cross-site advertising or browsing profiles

The public Website is primarily a static-first website.

### B. Administrative CMS Dashboard (`dash.renderphoenix.com`)
For authorized studio administrators, editors, and team members who access the private CMS dashboard at `dash.renderphoenix.com`:

- **Authentication Credentials:** Admin usernames and securely hashed passwords used strictly to authenticate authorized studio personnel.
- **Session & Security Information:** Temporary authentication session tokens, login timestamps, and security access logs required to maintain authenticated sessions and protect content management workflows.
- **Content Management Data:** Project showcases, devlog articles, media asset metadata, and editorial drafts created or edited by administrators for publication.

Administrative login access is strictly restricted to authorized RenderPhoenix studio team members and is not open to public registration.

However, certain third-party services used by or connected to the Website (such as Cloudflare DNS and Cloudflare Web Analytics) may independently process technical information. This is explained later in this Privacy Policy.

---

# 5. Information You May Voluntarily Provide

Although normal Website browsing does not require personal information, you may voluntarily provide information when communicating with RenderPhoenix.

For example, you may contact us regarding:

- A project
- Game development
- Collaboration
- Content submission
- Copyright concerns
- DMCA or copyright infringement reports
- Privacy questions
- Business inquiries
- Sponsorship inquiries
- Media inquiries
- Technical questions
- General communication
- Other legitimate matters

If you voluntarily contact us, the information you provide may include:

- Your name
- Your email address
- The content of your message
- Project information
- Information you voluntarily include in your message
- Information voluntarily provided in connection with a collaboration or content submission

We only intend to request basic information necessary to communicate with you.

---

# 6. Contact Form

RenderPhoenix may provide a contact form on the Website.

The intended contact form fields are limited to:

- Name
- Email address
- Message

At the effective date of this Privacy Policy, the contact form infrastructure has not yet been fully configured.

When the contact form is implemented, RenderPhoenix expects to use Google's email ecosystem, including Gmail, Google Workspace, Gmail-related services, and/or Google Apps Script or related Google technologies, depending on the final implementation.

The contact form is not intended to create a permanent user account or user profile.

RenderPhoenix does not intend to store contact submissions in a dedicated Website database.

Instead, messages may be transmitted to and handled through the email system used by RenderPhoenix.

---

# 7. Contact Information Retention

When you contact RenderPhoenix, we may retain the communication for as long as reasonably necessary to:

- Respond to your request
- Continue a project discussion
- Complete a collaboration
- Resolve a technical or copyright issue
- Maintain necessary business records
- Address disputes
- Protect our legal rights
- Comply with applicable legal obligations

When the purpose for retaining a communication has ended, RenderPhoenix intends to delete or otherwise remove the information when reasonably practical.

We do not intend to retain personal contact information indefinitely without a legitimate reason.

However, we may retain limited information for longer where reasonably necessary because of:

- Legal obligations
- Ongoing disputes
- Copyright or intellectual-property matters
- Security issues
- Fraud prevention
- Legal claims
- Requests from competent authorities
- Establishing, exercising, or defending legal rights

If you request deletion of your information, we will make reasonable efforts to honor the request, subject to legitimate legal, security, or operational reasons for retaining certain information.

---

# 8. Email Communication

If you contact RenderPhoenix by email or through a future contact form, your message may be processed through Google's email infrastructure.

RenderPhoenix currently intends to use the Google ecosystem for its official contact email and related communication services.

This means that Google may process information associated with email delivery and storage according to Google's own services and policies.

RenderPhoenix does not operate its own independent email server infrastructure for this purpose.

We do not intend to sell, rent, or commercially trade email addresses obtained through direct communications.

We also do not intend to use contact emails for unrelated advertising campaigns.

---

# 9. Automatic Replies

RenderPhoenix may implement an automated confirmation or acknowledgment email when the contact form becomes operational.

If implemented, such an email may confirm that:

- Your message was received
- Your request is being reviewed
- You may receive a response from the RenderPhoenix team

Automated email processing may be performed using Google services or Google Apps Script.

An automated reply does not create a user account or advertising profile.

---

# 10. Information We Do Not Request

RenderPhoenix strongly discourages visitors from submitting sensitive or unnecessary personal information through contact forms, emails, project submissions, or other communication channels.

You should **not** submit information such as:

- Passwords
- Authentication credentials
- Credit card numbers
- Bank account information
- Government identification numbers
- Passport information
- National identification numbers
- Medical information
- Health records
- Private photographs unrelated to the request
- Biometric information
- Precise private location information
- Highly sensitive personal information
- Confidential credentials
- Security keys
- API keys
- Private encryption keys
- Recovery codes
- Other information that you would not normally want shared through an ordinary business contact channel

RenderPhoenix does not request such information through its Website contact functionality.

If you voluntarily send such information despite these warnings, RenderPhoenix will handle it as reasonably necessary and may delete it when practical.

If the information creates a legal, security, or safety concern, additional retention or handling may be necessary.

---

# 11. User Accounts and Administrative CMS Login

### A. Public Visitors (No Public User Accounts)
RenderPhoenix does not operate public user registration or public login functionality on the Website.

You do not need to create an account to browse the Website.

The public Website does not provide:

- Public user registration
- Public user login
- Public password authentication
- Public user profiles
- Public user dashboards
- Personal libraries or saved user content

RenderPhoenix has no intention of requiring user accounts merely to access normal project, blog, or portfolio content.

### B. Administrative CMS Dashboard (`dash.renderphoenix.com`)
RenderPhoenix operates an administrative Content Management System (CMS) portal hosted at `dash.renderphoenix.com` strictly for internal studio administration.

- Authorized studio administrators and content creators log into this dashboard with designated administrator usernames and passwords to create, draft, edit, and publish devlog articles, project showcases, and website content.
- This CMS dashboard is private and intended solely for authorized studio staff. It does not provide public user registration, public reader accounts, or public visitor dashboards.
- Authentication credentials and session tokens used on `dash.renderphoenix.com` are processed and stored securely for the sole purpose of authenticating administrative staff and maintaining site content integrity.

---

# 12. Databases and Content Management

RenderPhoenix does not operate a general-purpose user tracking database for public Website visitors.

The Website is designed without a system that continuously builds profiles containing visitor information.

We do not intentionally create a database containing:

- Public visitor names or emails
- Public visitor browsing histories or behavioral records
- Public visitor interests or preferences
- Individual visitor download histories
- Public visitor tracking profiles

For internal studio operations, RenderPhoenix maintains administrative databases and content repositories used exclusively by the CMS (`dash.renderphoenix.com`) to store:

- Published and drafted blog posts and devlogs
- Project portfolio information and specifications
- Studio media asset references
- Authorized administrator account credentials and authentication session records

Contact communications may exist in the email systems used to communicate with RenderPhoenix, but this is kept completely separate from public Website browsing.

---

# 13. Cookies and Local Storage

### A. Public Website Browsing
RenderPhoenix does not operate a cookie-based user tracking system for public visitors.

The public Website does not use cookies or local storage for:

- Public visitor profiling
- Cross-site behavioral tracking
- Tracking individual project downloads
- Building advertising audiences directly by RenderPhoenix

### B. Administrative Dashboard (`dash.renderphoenix.com`)
The administrative CMS dashboard at `dash.renderphoenix.com` may use essential session cookies, local storage tokens, or security cookies strictly necessary to maintain authenticated administrator sessions, remember login states, and protect against cross-site request forgery. These essential technical cookies are restricted to the administrative portal and are never used for marketing, advertising, or tracking public visitors.

### C. Third-Party Services
Third-party services embedded in or connected to the Website (such as YouTube or future advertising providers) may use cookies, local storage, pixels, identifiers, or similar technologies according to their own systems.

This may become particularly relevant if RenderPhoenix activates advertising services such as Google AdSense.

If advertising or another third-party service requires cookies or similar technologies, RenderPhoenix will implement the appropriate consent mechanism and configuration required by applicable laws and the relevant service provider.

---

RenderPhoenix intends to monetize the Website through advertising in the future, including Google AdSense or other Google advertising products where appropriate.

At the effective date of this Privacy Policy, advertising may not yet be active.

When advertising is activated, advertising providers may use technologies such as:

- Cookies
- Local storage
- Advertising identifiers
- IP address
- Browser information
- Device information

- Website interaction signals
- Advertising-related identifiers
- Other technical or advertising information permitted under applicable policies and laws

The specific information processed may depend on:

- The advertising provider
- The visitor's location
- The visitor's consent choices
- The type of advertisement
- Browser settings
- Device settings
- Applicable laws
- Advertising configuration
- Third-party technology

RenderPhoenix does not independently control every category of information that Google or another advertising provider may process when advertising is displayed.

Where applicable, advertising providers may use information to provide personalized or non-personalized advertising.

RenderPhoenix intends to follow the applicable requirements of Google and relevant privacy laws when advertising is activated.

Where applicable law requires consent before certain advertising technologies or personalized advertising can be used, RenderPhoenix intends to implement the appropriate consent mechanism.

This may include a Google-certified Consent Management Platform or another consent mechanism required or recommended by Google and applicable regulations.

The availability and behavior of advertising may vary depending on:

- Country
- Region
- Applicable law
- Consent status
- Advertising configuration

- Device settings

Visitors may be presented with privacy or advertising choices where required.

RenderPhoenix does not intend to bypass legally required consent mechanisms.

We will configure advertising services according to the applicable requirements in effect when those services are implemented.

# 16. Personalized Advertising

If Google AdSense or another advertising service provides personalized advertising, the advertising provider may process information necessary for advertising personalization according to its own policies and applicable laws.

RenderPhoenix does not intend to manually build advertising profiles of Website visitors.

RenderPhoenix also does not intend to upload contact-form users or newsletter subscribers to advertising systems to create advertising audiences.

Contact information provided for communication or newsletter purposes is intended to remain separate from advertising audience creation.

# 17. Web Analytics and Traffic Monitoring

### A. Cloudflare Web Analytics
RenderPhoenix uses **Cloudflare Web Analytics** across the Website to monitor aggregate traffic, page views, and technical performance (including Core Web Vitals and page load speed).

Cloudflare Web Analytics is deployed via a lightweight, client-side JavaScript beacon snippet (`beacon.min.js`, token: `e70dd5ade19f4847b5cdfb088dafc1db`).

Cloudflare Web Analytics is built with a privacy-first approach:

- **No Cookies or Local Storage:** It does not use client-side cookies or local storage to track visitors.
- **No Cross-Site Tracking:** It does not follow or track individual visitors across different websites.
- **No Personal Profiling:** It does not collect personally identifiable information (PII), visitor names, or create personal browsing profiles.
- **Aggregated Performance Metrics:** It provides RenderPhoenix with high-level, privacy-preserving aggregate metrics (such as total page impressions, top referrer domains, visitor country of origin, browser types, and web performance timings).

### B. Google Analytics
RenderPhoenix does not currently use Google Analytics as a Website analytics system.

### C. Google Search Console
RenderPhoenix uses Google Search Console to monitor search indexing and search engine visibility. Search Console provides aggregate search performance metrics and does not provide personally identifiable visitor records.

---

# 18. Google Search Console

RenderPhoenix may use Google Search Console to monitor the Website's performance in Google Search.

Search Console may provide information such as:

- Search queries
- Search impressions
- Search clicks
- Search positions
- Indexed pages
- Search visibility
- Technical search information
- Website performance information

RenderPhoenix uses this information primarily to understand and improve the Website's search visibility, indexing, technical health, and content performance.

Search Console does not give RenderPhoenix a general-purpose database of personally identifiable Website visitors.

Google independently processes information associated with its services according to Google's own policies.

# 19. Google Fonts

RenderPhoenix may use Google Fonts.

That communication may involve technical information such as an IP address or browser-related information as determined by Google's infrastructure.

RenderPhoenix does not use Google Fonts to build visitor profiles.

This may include information associated with:

- Browser requests
- Device information
- IP address
- Video interaction
- Cookies or similar technologies
- Other technical information

The handling of this information is controlled by Google and YouTube's applicable policies and technologies.

RenderPhoenix does not receive a private database containing the personal information of every person who watches an embedded video.

---

# 24. Cloudflare DNS and Proxy Infrastructure

RenderPhoenix uses **Cloudflare** for authoritative DNS routing, reverse proxy (CDN), edge security, and network infrastructure across its domains and subdomains (including `renderphoenix.com` and `dash.renderphoenix.com`).

- **Cloudflare DNS & Proxy Active:** Cloudflare DNS and proxying are enabled to route web traffic through Cloudflare's global edge network, providing fast Anycast domain resolution, CDN edge caching, DDoS mitigation, web application firewall (WAF) protections, and end-to-end SSL/TLS security encryption.
- **Technical Request Processing:** When web requests pass through Cloudflare's proxy servers to reach our origin hosting, Cloudflare necessarily processes technical request metadata (such as IP addresses, HTTP request headers, and connection telemetry) strictly for traffic routing, security filtering, and threat detection.
- **No Visitor Profiling:** RenderPhoenix does not use Cloudflare DNS or proxy infrastructure to build personal visitor profiles, track individuals across third-party websites, or sell user data.
- Cloudflare processes network and security telemetry in accordance with Cloudflare's Privacy Policy and standard data protection terms.

---

# 25. External Download Platforms

RenderPhoenix generally does not operate a centralized download server containing personal user accounts or download histories.

Instead, project pages may link or redirect visitors to external platforms where the relevant files or applications are hosted.

# 26. RenderPhoenix Redirect Links

RenderPhoenix may use convenient redirect URLs such as:

`/dl/...`

These links may redirect a visitor from a RenderPhoenix URL to an external download destination.

The purpose of these links is primarily:

- Link management
- Maintaining stable public URLs
- Making links easier to update
- Redirecting visitors to the appropriate external download platform

RenderPhoenix does not intend to use these redirects as a personal tracking system.

We do not intend to use download redirect links to create individual visitor profiles.

A destination platform may nevertheless independently process technical information after the visitor reaches that platform.

# 35. Copyright and DMCA Requests

RenderPhoenix maintains a copyright and DMCA-related reporting process.

If you believe that content published on or through RenderPhoenix infringes your copyright or other intellectual-property rights, you may contact:

**[contact@renderphoenix.com](mailto:contact@renderphoenix.com)**

RenderPhoenix may request information reasonably necessary to investigate a copyright complaint.

This may include:

- Your name
- Contact information
- Identification of the copyrighted work
- Identification of the allegedly infringing material
- Explanation of the claim
- Supporting information
- Other information reasonably necessary to evaluate the complaint

Information submitted in connection with a legal complaint may need to be retained for legal or dispute-resolution purposes.

RenderPhoenix may also share information when reasonably necessary to investigate or respond to a legitimate legal claim.

---

# 36. Legal Disclosure

RenderPhoenix may disclose information where reasonably necessary to:

- Comply with applicable law
- Respond to lawful legal process
- Respond to court orders
- Respond to valid governmental requests
- Establish, exercise, or defend legal rights
- Investigate suspected fraud
- Address security incidents
- Protect the Website
- Protect users
- Protect RenderPhoenix
- Resolve disputes
- Prevent abuse or unlawful activity

RenderPhoenix will not intentionally disclose personal information simply because it is convenient to do so.

Where legally permitted and reasonably appropriate, RenderPhoenix will consider the necessity and proportionality of such disclosure.

---

# 37. Legal Retention

Although RenderPhoenix generally intends to delete contact information when the purpose for retaining it has ended, certain information may need to be retained where reasonably necessary for legal purposes.

For example, information may be retained where it is relevant to:

- A copyright dispute
- A legal claim
- A contractual dispute
- Fraud investigation
- Security investigation
- Regulatory requirements
- Legal proceedings
- Protection of RenderPhoenix's rights

Once the relevant legal or operational reason no longer exists, RenderPhoenix intends to delete or anonymize the information when reasonably practical.

# 38. Sale or Transfer of the Studio

RenderPhoenix does not intend to sell, rent, or trade personal information.

If RenderPhoenix itself is reorganized, acquired, merged, or transferred as part of a legitimate business transaction, information may need to be handled as part of that transaction where legally permitted.

However, RenderPhoenix does not intend to treat user personal information as a commercial product to be sold independently.

Any future transfer involving personal information will be handled in accordance with applicable laws and contractual obligations.

# 39. Children's Privacy

The RenderPhoenix Website is intended for a general audience, including gamers and game developers.

The Website is **not specifically designed or marketed as a children-only service** and is not intended to function as a child-directed platform.

However, games, Minecraft projects, and other entertainment content published by RenderPhoenix may naturally be used or viewed by people of different ages, including children.

RenderPhoenix does not intentionally require children to provide personal information to browse ordinary Website content.

RenderPhoenix does not knowingly seek to build profiles of children.

RenderPhoenix does not intentionally request sensitive personal information from children.

If a child chooses to contact RenderPhoenix, the same privacy principles described in this Privacy Policy apply.

We strongly discourage anyone, including children, from submitting passwords, financial information, government identification, health information, or other sensitive information through the Website's contact channels.

If RenderPhoenix becomes aware that it has received personal information from a child in circumstances where such information should not have been collected, RenderPhoenix will consider appropriate steps to delete or otherwise handle the information in accordance with applicable law.

If a user voluntarily provides sensitive information in a message, RenderPhoenix may delete it where reasonably practical unless there is a legitimate reason to retain it.

# 41. Data Security

RenderPhoenix does not operate a public user-account database or large-scale personal-information system for public visitors.

Because of this architecture, the public Website does not maintain public user password databases, user profile databases, payment databases, or visitor tracking databases.

For the administrative CMS dashboard (`dash.renderphoenix.com`), administrative access is protected through:

- Secure password hashing and authentication controls
- Role-based administrative access restricted to authorized studio personnel
- HTTPS/TLS encryption for all administrative sessions and data transmission
- Session timeout and secure cookie/token handling

For communications received via email or contact channels, RenderPhoenix applies reasonable technical and organizational safeguards:

- Access controls and strong authentication for official studio accounts
- Limited internal access to authorized team members only
- Avoiding unnecessary data collection
- Deleting information when no longer needed
- Using reputable infrastructure providers (e.g., GitHub, Cloudflare, Google)
- Keeping Website infrastructure reasonably maintained

No online service can guarantee absolute security. RenderPhoenix therefore cannot promise that information transmitted over the Internet will always remain completely secure, but we take diligent measures to protect our systems.

---

# 42. No Absolute Security Guarantee

Although RenderPhoenix takes reasonable measures to avoid unnecessary data collection and protect information it receives, no Internet transmission, email system, hosting platform, or third-party service can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

RenderPhoenix therefore cannot guarantee:

- Absolute security
- Absolute confidentiality
- Zero risk of unauthorized access
- Zero risk of third-party service incidents
- Zero risk of Internet interception
- Zero risk of technical failure

The most effective privacy measure used by RenderPhoenix is minimizing the amount of information collected in the first place.

---

# 43. Data Minimization

RenderPhoenix follows a data-minimization approach.

This means that we generally aim to collect or retain only information reasonably necessary for a specific purpose.

For example, a contact request generally requires:

- Name
- Email
- Message

It does not require:

- Password
- Phone number
- Home address
- Government ID
- Payment information
- Precise location
- Date of birth
- Sensitive personal information

We do not ask for information merely because it might be useful someday.

---

# 44. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on where you live and which laws apply to you, you may have rights concerning personal information processed by RenderPhoenix.

These rights may include, where applicable:

- The right to ask whether we process your information
- The right to request access to information we hold about you
- The right to request correction of inaccurate information
- The right to request deletion
- The right to object to certain processing
- The right to restrict certain processing
- The right to withdraw consent where processing relies on consent
- The right to request information about how your information is used
- Other rights provided by applicable law

RenderPhoenix will consider reasonable privacy requests.

Because RenderPhoenix does not maintain a conventional user database, there may be situations where we have no information associated with a particular visitor.

---

# 45. How to Make a Privacy Request

For privacy-related questions or requests, contact:

**[contact@renderphoenix.com](mailto:contact@renderphoenix.com)**

You may request:

- Information about data we may hold
- Correction
- Deletion
- Clarification about processing
- Information about a contact submission
- Questions about this Privacy Policy
- Questions about third-party services

To protect users from unauthorized requests, RenderPhoenix may need to take reasonable steps to verify the identity or authority of a person making a request.

If we cannot verify that a request is genuinely associated with the relevant person, we may be unable to fulfill the request.

---

# 46. Deletion Requests

RenderPhoenix supports reasonable deletion requests.

If you ask us to delete information associated with your communication, we will generally make reasonable efforts to remove it when the information is no longer necessary.

However, deletion may not be absolute where information must reasonably be retained for:

- Legal obligations
- Legal claims
- Copyright disputes
- Security investigations
- Fraud prevention
- Establishing or defending legal rights
- Other legitimate legal purposes

If certain information cannot be deleted for one of these reasons, RenderPhoenix will seek to limit its use to the purpose requiring retention where reasonably practical.
